title: Extraction from equality-free first-order Harrop assumptions

based_on.title: Proof Theory 2018: Sequent calculus for predicate logic (handout 9)
based_on.pages: Ch.13, printed pp.1–4: equality-free rules and syntactic existence property; Harrop-context extension developed locally

summary: Extract disjuncts and witnesses from actual equality-free deductions under Harrop assumptions, and move a fresh existential outside a Harrop premise with precise term conditions.
abstract: A proof of an existential statement may still reveal a witness when some assumptions remain open. Harrop assumptions describe one useful class: they allow universal formulas and implications with complicated inputs, but exclude disjunctions and existential quantifiers from their direct output. We follow the conclusion through a supplied equality-free proof and rebuild its remaining left rules. A disjunction gives a definite proved side. An existential gives either a term with a proof of its instance or a proof that the assumptions contradict one another. Consistency removes the latter possibility, while a supplied original term handles it by explosion. Public proofs have reserved parameter names available; keeping those names visible explains both their stronger witness result and the conditions for returning to the original names. These constructions also move a fresh existential outside a Harrop premise: raw proofs require an original term or consistency of the enlarged context, while public proofs use their reserve.
